deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a pencil note of a lecture timetable. The days are German abbreviations (Mo. = Montag, Dienst. = Dienstag, Mittw. = Mittwoch, Donnerst., Freit., Sonnabends). The hours are Roman numerals: II-III = 2-3 o'clock, I-II = 1-2, X = 10, XI = 11. The entries are:

(1) Weber, II-IV (2-4 o'clock), Monday and Wednesday. A deleted word follows; possibly 'Licht' or similar. This is Wilhelm Weber's physics lecture.

(2) Dirichlet: 'Zahlentheorie' (number theory), Mon/Tue/Wed II-III. Deleted: Donnerst./Freitag. Also 'part. Diff.' (partielle Differentialgleichungen, partial differential equations), Mon/Tue/Wed/Thu I-II. Also, added at upper right, 'Donnerst. Freit. Sonnabends II-III' (Thu/Fri/Sat 2-3).

(3) Stern (Moritz Abraham Stern): 'Anal. et geom.' (analysis and geometry, perhaps analytic geometry), XI (11 o'clock). Also 'Th. aeq. num.' (Theoria aequationum numericarum, theory of numerical equations), X (10 o'clock).

(4) A free-standing '11-12', plausibly a slot Riemann was considering for his own course so as to avoid clashes.

At the foot, written upside down relative to the page, is a line in German cursive. It looks like a draft of the opening sentence on the next page ('Die Aufgabe, deren Lösung der Zweck dieser Vorlesungen ... gegebener ...'), preceded by 'gesch.' or similar.

Dating context (my inference): Dirichlet taught in Göttingen only from 1855, where Weber and Stern were colleagues. This suggests the sheet is a Göttingen semester timetable from c. 1855-1859, during Riemann's time as Privatdozent. The next page begins Riemann's own lecture on functions of a complex variable (introduction; Cauchy integral theorem via the condition dX/dy - dY/dx = 0). That fits Riemann planning his lecture hour (11-12?) around his colleagues' courses. The bundle label '1850' would then be loose, unless the Dirichlet entries refer to something else.
